claim: The Spemann organizer can induce a secondary body axis when grafted to the ventral side of a host gastrula embryo in amphibians.
source: They found that by grafting the dorsal-lip of an amphibian embryo (now known as the Spemann Organizer) to the ventral side of the host gastrula embryo it was possible to induce a secondary body axis (Spemann and Mangold, 2001; De Robertis, 2009; Anderson and Stern, 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published work (Spemann and Mangold, 2001; De Robertis, 2009; Anderson and Stern, 2016).

claim: Spider embryos have high self-regulatory capacities that can result in spontaneous twinning.
source: Intriguingly, spider embryos also have high self-regulatory capacities, even to the extent that twinning can occur spontaneously (Napiórkowska et al., 2016; Oda and Akiyama-Oda, 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published work (Napiórkowska et al., 2016; Oda and Akiyama-Oda, 2008).

claim: The cumulus is needed to break the radial symmetry of the early spider embryo and to induce the dorsoventral body axis.
source: During spider embryogenesis a group of migratory cells (the cumulus) is needed to break the radial symmetry of the early embryo and to induce the dorsoventral body axis (Oda and Akiyama-Oda, 2008; Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2003, 2006; McGregor et al., 2008; Hilbrant et al., 2012; Mittmann and Wolff, 2012; Schwager et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published work (Oda and Akiyama-Oda, 2008; Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2003, 2006; McGregor et al., 2008; Hilbrant et al., 2012; Mittmann and Wolff, 2012; Schwager et al., 2015).

claim: Transplanting cumulus material can induce a secondary axis in spider embryos.
source: Similar to the vertebrate experiments, Holm showed that transplanting cumulus material was able to induce a secondary axis in spider embryos (Holm, 1952).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published work (Holm, 1952).

claim: The cumulus signals via BMP signaling.
source: Modern work has shown that the cumulus signals via BMP signaling (again, similar to vertebrates).
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to modern work and established scientific knowledge.

claim: The mesenchymal cumulus cells are the source of the BMP receptor ligand Decapentaplegic.
source: The mesenchymal cumulus cells are the source of the BMP receptor ligand Decapentaplegic (Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published work (Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2006).

claim: Interfering with the BMP signaling pathway by gene knockdown results in the loss of dorsal tissue identity and leads to completely radially-symmetric and ventralized embryos.
source: Interfering with the BMP signaling pathway by gene knockdown results in the loss of dorsal tissue identity, which in turn leads to completely radially-symmetric and ventralized embryos (Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published work (Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2006).

claim: The cumulus forms in the center of the germ-disc and migrates underneath the ectoderm towards the rim of the disc.
source: The cumulus forms in the center of the so-called germ-disc (the embryonic pole of the embryo) and migrates underneath the ectoderm towards the rim of the disc.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published work (Oda and Akiyama-Oda, 2008; Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2003, 2006; McGregor et al., 2008; Hilbrant et al., 2012; Mittmann and Wolff, 2012; Schwager et al., 2015).

claim: Arrival of the cumulus at the rim induces the opening of the germ-disc.
source: Arrival of the cumulus at the rim induces the opening of the germ-disc (Oda and Akiyama-Oda, 2008; Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2003, 2006; McGregor et al., 2008; Hilbrant et al., 2012; Mittmann and Wolff, 2012; Schwager et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published work (Oda and Akiyama-Oda, 2008; Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2003, 2006; McGregor et al., 2008; Hilbrant et al., 2012; Mittmann and Wolff, 2012; Schwager et al., 2015).

claim: Cumulus migration is dependent on the Hh-signaling pathway.
source: Cumulus migration is dependent on the Hh-signaling pathway (Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2010)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published work (Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2010).

claim: Knockdown of components of the Hh-signaling pathway results in cumulus migration defects and in the ectopic opening of the germ-disc.
source: it was shown that the knockdown of components of this signaling pathway results in cumulus migration defects and in the ectopic opening of the germ-disc (Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published work (Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2010).

claim: During the formation of the germ-disc a small cluster of cells ingress and form an indentation where the future center of the fully formed germ-disc will be located.
source: During the formation of the germ-disc a small cluster of cells ingress and form an indentation where the future center of the fully formed germ-disc will be located.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published work (Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2003; Hilbrant et al., 2012).

claim: The cluster of cells that forms an indentation during germ-disc formation appears as a visible spot called the primary thickening.
source: This cluster of cells appears as a visible spot and is called the primary thickening (Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2003; Hilbrant et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published work (Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2003; Hilbrant et al., 2012).

claim: It is not clear whether all or only a subset of the cells of the primary thickening give rise to the cumulus, or if cumulus cells arise from subsequent cell invagination at the site of the primary thickening.
source: However, it is not clear whether all or only a subset of the cells of the primary thickening give rise to the cumulus, or if cumulus cells arise from subsequent cell invagination at the site of the primary thickening (Oda and Akiyama-Oda, 2008; Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published work (Oda and Akiyama-Oda, 2008; Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2003).

claim: Cell tracing and the expression of the endodermal marker forkhead within the primary thickening/cumulus cells led to the suggestion that the primary thickening/cumulus cells are central endodermal cells.
source: Cell tracing (Holm, 1952; Edgar et al., 2015), as well as the expression of the endodermal marker forkhead (Oda et al., 2007) within the primary thickening/cumulus cells led to the suggestion that the primary thickening/cumulus cells are central endodermal cells (Hilbrant et al., 2012; Oda et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published work (Holm, 1952; Edgar et al., 2015; Oda et al., 2007; Hilbrant et al., 2012).

claim: Studies could not completely rule out that the labeled cumulus cells develop into cells of the visceral mesoderm.
source: However, these studies could not completely rule out that the labeled cumulus cells develop into cells of the visceral mesoderm (Edgar et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published work (Edgar et al., 2015).

claim: The transcriptome sequencing of carefully staged embryos was carried out to find new genes involved in cumulus and axial patterning in the spider Parasteatoda tepidariorum.
source: To overcome the limitations of the candidate gene approach, we have carried out transcriptome sequencing of carefully staged embryos to find new genes involved in cumulus and axial patterning in the spider Parasteatoda tepidariorum.
evidence: The claim is supported by the description of the experimental approach in the manuscript.

claim: Pt-Ets4 was identified as a new gene expressed during early development and is expressed exclusively within the central primary thickening and the cells of the migrating cumulus.
source: From this work, we have identified the transcription factor Pt-Ets4 as a new gene expressed during early development and have found it to be expressed exclusively within the central primary thickening and the cells of the migrating cumulus.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Pt-Ets4 is needed for the integrity of the cumulus.
source: Our combined genetic and cellular analyses show that Pt-Ets4 is needed for the integrity of the cumulus.
evidence: The claim is supported by the genetic and cellular analyses presented in the manuscript.

claim: The knockdown of Pt-Ets4 leads to embryos that show axis patterning defects reminiscent of BMP knockdown phenotypes.
source: We found that the knockdown of this gene leads to embryos that show axis patterning defects reminiscent of BMP knockdown phenotypes, suggesting that an intact cumulus is needed to induce the formation of the bilaterally symmetric spider embryo.
evidence: The claim is supported by the knockdown experiments presented in the manuscript.

claim: An intact cumulus is needed to induce the formation of the bilaterally symmetric spider embryo.
source: We found that the knockdown of this gene leads to embryos that show axis patterning defects reminiscent of BMP knockdown phenotypes, suggesting that an intact cumulus is needed to induce the formation of the bilaterally symmetric spider embryo.
evidence: The claim is supported by inference from the knockdown experiments presented in the manuscript.

claim: Pt-Ets4 is necessary and sufficient for driving the early expression of twist and hunchback.
source: Importantly, Pt-Ets4 is necessary and sufficient for driving the early expression of twist (a gene involved in gastrulation and mesoderm formation in Drosophila) and hunchback
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Ectopic expression of Pt-Ets4 is sufficient to induce cell delamination.
source: and the ectopic expression of Pt-Ets4 is sufficient to induce cell delamination.
evidence: The claim is supported by the ectopic expression experiments presented in the manuscript.

claim: The formation of the germ-disc is one of the most important events during spider embryogenesis.
source: The formation of the germ-disc is one of the most important events during spider embryogenesis.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge in the field.

claim: A regular blastoderm with no visible axial polarity is present at stage 2.
source: While a regular blastoderm (with no visible axial polarity) is present at stage 2, the germ-disc condenses during stage 3 of embryonic development (Figure 1A and B, for detailed description see [Pechmann, 2016]).
evidence: The claim is supported by the description in the text and reference to Figure 1A and B, as well as a citation to Pechmann, 2016.

claim: The germ-disc condenses during stage 3 of embryonic development.
source: While a regular blastoderm (with no visible axial polarity) is present at stage 2, the germ-disc condenses during stage 3 of embryonic development (Figure 1A and B, for detailed description see [Pechmann, 2016]).
evidence: The claim is supported by the description in the text and reference to Figure 1A and B, as well as a citation to Pechmann, 2016.

claim: Germ-disc condensation leads to the establishment of the anterior/posterior body axis.
source: This event leads to the establishment of the anterior/posterior body axis (anterior: rim of the disc; posterior: center of the disc).
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge in the field.

claim: Pt-Ets4 is expressed within the cluster of cells that will develop into the central primary thickening.
source: (A and B) Pt-Ets4 is expressed within the cluster of cells (arrow in A) that will develop into the central primary thickening (pt) (B).
evidence: The claim is supported by the description in the text and reference to Figure 1A and B.

claim: Pt-Ets4 is expressed within the primary thickening and in the migrating cumulus, which are covered by the surface epithelium of the germ-disc.
source: (C–D') Confocal scans (single optical slices (C and D'); maximum intensity projection (D)) of embryos stained for Pt-Ets4 (FastRed stain; red) and nuclei (DAPI; blue). Pt-Ets4 is expressed within the primary thickening and in the migrating cumulus (cu), which are covered by the surface epithelium of the germ-disc.
evidence: The claim is supported by the description in the text and reference to Figure 1C-D'.

claim: Pt-Ets4 has high similarity to Drosophila melanogaster Ets4/Ets98B.
source: One of the candidates was an Ets-like gene with high similarity to Drosophila melanogaster Ets4/Ets98B (see Figure 1—figure supplement 2), henceforth called Parasteatoda tepidariorum Ets4 (Pt-Ets4).
evidence: The claim is supported by the description in the text and reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Prior to germ-disc condensation, Pt-Ets4 is expressed within the cluster of cells that will form the center of the future germ-disc at early stage 3.
source: Prior to germ-disc condensation, Pt-Ets4 is expressed within the cluster of cells that will form the center of the future germ-disc at early stage 3 (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by the description in the text and reference to Figure 1A.

claim: At stage 4, Pt-Ets4 is strongly and exclusively expressed within the central cluster of cells (the primary thickening) that has delaminated during germ-disc formation.
source: Expression persists throughout germ-disc formation and, at stage 4, Pt-Ets4 is strongly and exclusively expressed within the central cluster of cells (the so-called primary thickening, Figure 1B) that has delaminated during germ-disc formation (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by the description in the text and reference to Figure 1B and 1C.

claim: During stage 5, the cumulus starts to migrate from the center of the germ-disc to its periphery.
source: During stage 5, the cumulus starts to migrate from the center of the germ-disc to its periphery (Oda and Akiyama-Oda, 2008; Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2003, 2006; McGregor et al., 2008; Hilbrant et al., 2012; Mittmann and Wolff, 2012; Schwager et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published work (Oda and Akiyama-Oda, 2008; Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2003, 2006; McGregor et al., 2008; Hilbrant et al., 2012; Mittmann and Wolff, 2012; Schwager et al., 2015).

claim: At stage 5, Pt-Ets4 is strongly and exclusively expressed in the migrating cumulus cells.
source: At this stage Pt-Ets4 is strongly and exclusively expressed in the migrating cumulus cells (Figure 1D and D').
evidence: The claim is supported by the description in the text and reference to Figure 1D and D'.

claim: Pt-Ets4 transcripts were not detected in ovaries and early stage 1 embryos via RNA in situ hybridization.
source: We were not able to detect Pt-Ets4 transcripts in ovaries and early stage 1 embryos via RNA in situ hybridization (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by the description in the text and reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 3A and B.

claim: Pt-Ets4 is only expressed at a very low level during early stage 1, but is mildly up-regulated at late stage 2 and strongly up-regulated at early stage 3.
source: In addition, our sequencing data shows that Pt-Ets4 is only expressed at a very low level during early stage 1, but is mildly up-regulated at late stage 2 and strongly up-regulated at early stage 3 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by the sequencing data presented in the manuscript and reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Pt-Ets4 transcripts are not maternally provided.
source: From this we conclude that Pt-Ets4 transcripts are not maternally provided.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the expression data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The knockdown of Pt-Ets4 did not affect formation of the germ-disc.
source: Time-lapse imaging and cross-sectioning revealed that the knockdown of Pt-Ets4 neither affected formation of the germ-disc nor of the primary thickening/cumulus (Video 1B; middle column in Figure 2, Figure 3A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by the time-lapse imaging and cross-sectioning data presented in the manuscript and reference to Video 1B, Figure 2, and Figure 3A and B.

claim: The knockdown of Pt-Ets4 did not affect formation of the primary thickening/cumulus.
source: Time-lapse imaging and cross-sectioning revealed that the knockdown of Pt-Ets4 neither affected formation of the germ-disc nor of the primary thickening/cumulus (Video 1B; middle column in Figure 2, Figure 3A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by the time-lapse imaging and cross-sectioning data presented in the manuscript and reference to Video 1B, Figure 2, and Figure 3A and B.

claim: During stage 5, cumulus integrity was affected in Pt-Ets4 knockdown embryos.
source: However, during stage 5, cumulus integrity was affected in Pt-Ets4 knockdown embryos (Video 1B, middle column in Figure 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by the time-lapse imaging data presented in the manuscript and reference to Video 1B and Figure 2.

claim: In control embryos the cumulus migrated towards the rim.
source: While in control embryos the cumulus migrated towards the rim (Video 1A, left column in Figure 2)
evidence: The claim is supported by the time-lapse imaging data presented in the manuscript and reference to Video 1A and Figure 2.

claim: The cumulus of Pt-Ets4 RNAi embryos remained at the center of the germ-disc until early stage 5 and disappeared soon after gastrulation was initiated at the center and at the rim of the disc.
source: the cumulus of Pt-Ets4 RNAi embryos remained at the center of the germ-disc until early stage 5 and disappeared soon after gastrulation was initiated at the center and at the rim of the disc (Video 1B (15h onwards), middle column in Figure 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by the time-lapse imaging data presented in the manuscript and reference to Video 1B and Figure 2.

claim: In mid-stage 5 Pt-Ets4 RNAi embryos, although the cells of the cumulus were still in the center of the germ-disc, they appeared to be more loosely organized.
source: Analysis of mid-stage 5 Pt-Ets4 RNAi embryos for the expression of the cumulus marker Pt-fascin (Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2010) revealed that although the cells of the cumulus were still in the center of the germ-disc, they appeared to be more loosely organized (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by the expression analysis data presented in the manuscript and reference to Figure 3C and D, as well as a citation to Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2010.

claim: In Pt-Ets4 knockdown embryos the radial symmetry of the germ-disc was not broken.
source: In Pt-Ets4 knockdown embryos the radial symmetry of the germ-disc was not broken (as shown by the formation of a tube-like germ band in Video 1B (30h onwards), and the middle column in Figure 2), presumably due to the loss of the cumulus.
evidence: The claim is supported by the time-lapse imaging data presented in the manuscript and reference to Video 1B and Figure 2.

claim: The radial symmetry of the germ-disc was not broken in Pt-Ets4 knockdown embryos presumably due to the loss of the cumulus.
source: In Pt-Ets4 knockdown embryos the radial symmetry of the germ-disc was not broken (as shown by the formation of a tube-like germ band in Video 1B (30h onwards), and the middle column in Figure 2), presumably due to the loss of the cumulus.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: In Pt-ptc knockdown embryos, cumulus migration is lost but the cumulus itself is otherwise unaffected.
source: To investigate this phenotype in more detail, we knocked down another gene that also results in defects in radial symmetry breaking, Pt-ptc. In Pt-ptc knockdown embryos, cumulus migration is lost but the cumulus itself is otherwise unaffected (Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published work (Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2010).

claim: After pRNAi with Pt-ptc, the cumulus stays in the center of the germ-disc.
source: After pRNAi with Pt-ptc, the cumulus stays in the center of the germ-disc (Video 1C; right column in Figure 2)
evidence: The claim is supported by the time-lapse imaging data presented in the manuscript and reference to Video 1C and Figure 2.

claim: After pRNAi with Pt-ptc, BMP signaling is ectopically activated.
source: and BMP signaling is ectopically activated (as shown via antibody staining against the phosphorylated form of mothers against dpp (pMAD) (Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2010)).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published work (Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2010).

claim: In Pt-ptc RNAi embryos, the germ-disc ectopically opened at the center and the dorsal field was induced at the posterior pole.
source: As a result, the germ-disc ectopically opened at the center and the dorsal field was induced at the posterior pole of the Pt-ptc RNAi embryos (right column in Figure 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by the imaging data presented in the manuscript and reference to Figure 2.

claim: Ectopic induction of the dorsal field in the center of the germ-disc was never observed in the Pt-Ets4 RNAi embryos.
source: This ectopic induction of the dorsal field in the center of the germ-disc was never observed in the Pt-Ets4 RNAi embryos.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental observations presented in the manuscript.

claim: In control embryos the cumulus reached the periphery of the germ-disc at late stage 5 and a strong pMAD staining was visible in the overlying ectodermal cells.
source: In control embryos the cumulus reached the periphery of the germ-disc at late stage 5 and a strong pMAD staining was visible in the overlying ectodermal cells (Figure 3E, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by the antibody staining data presented in the manuscript and reference to Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: At late stage 5, the anterior marker Pt-orthodenticle (Pt-otd) was expressed in a ring, which had a width of 3–5 cells.
source: At this stage, the anterior marker Pt-orthodenticle (Pt-otd) was expressed in a ring, which had a width of 3–5 cells (Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2003; Pechmann et al., 2009; Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2016) (Figure 3E).
evidence: The claim is supported by the expression data presented in the manuscript and reference to Figure 3E, as well as citations to published work (Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2003; Pechmann et al., 2009; Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2016).

claim: In Pt-Ets4 knockdown embryos Pt-otd expression was unaffected but nuclear pMAD was not detectable.
source: In Pt-Ets4 knockdown embryos Pt-otd expression was unaffected but nuclear pMAD was not detectable (Figure 3F).
evidence: The claim is supported by the expression and antibody staining data presented in the manuscript and reference to Figure 3F.

claim: The lack of BMP signaling explains why Pt-Ets4 RNAi embryos do not induce the dorsal field and stay radially symmetric.
source: This lack of BMP signaling explains why Pt-Ets4 RNAi embryos do not induce the dorsal field and stay radially symmetric.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The Pt-Ets4 knockdown embryos were completely ventralized.
source: Indeed, the knockdown embryos were completely ventralized; the expression of the ventral marker Pt-short-gastrulation (Pt-sog) was uniform around the embryonic circumference and the segmental marker Pt-engrailed (Pt-en) was expressed in symmetric rings demonstrating the radial symmetry of the embryo (Figure 3G–L).
evidence: The claim is supported by the expression data presented in the manuscript and reference to Figure 3G–L.

claim: The expression of the ventral marker Pt-short-gastrulation (Pt-sog) was uniform around the embryonic circumference in Pt-Ets4 knockdown embryos.
source: Indeed, the knockdown embryos were completely ventralized; the expression of the ventral marker Pt-short-gastrulation (Pt-sog) was uniform around the embryonic circumference and the segmental marker Pt-engrailed (Pt-en) was expressed in symmetric rings demonstrating the radial symmetry of the embryo (Figure 3G–L).
evidence: The claim is supported by the expression data presented in the manuscript and reference to Figure 3G–L.

claim: The segmental marker Pt-engrailed (Pt-en) was expressed in symmetric rings in Pt-Ets4 knockdown embryos, demonstrating the radial symmetry of the embryo.
source: Indeed, the knockdown embryos were completely ventralized; the expression of the ventral marker Pt-short-gastrulation (Pt-sog) was uniform around the embryonic circumference and the segmental marker Pt-engrailed (Pt-en) was expressed in symmetric rings demonstrating the radial symmetry of the embryo (Figure 3G–L).
evidence: The claim is supported by the expression data presented in the manuscript and reference to Figure 3G–L.

claim: During later development the embryonic tissue of Pt-Ets4 knockdown embryos either grew completely over the yolk or a tube like structure elongated at the posterior of the embryo.
source: During later development the embryonic tissue either grew completely over the yolk (Figure 3J–L), or a tube like structure elongated at the posterior of the embryo (Video 1B, middle column Figure 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by the imaging data presented in the manuscript and reference to Figure 3J–L, Video 1B, and Figure 2.

claim: In Pt-ptc RNAi embryos, the germ-disc opened up centrally and a tube like structure formed at the anterior of the embryo.
source: This was in contrast to Pt-ptc RNAi embryos, where the germ-disc opened up centrally and a tube like structure formed at the anterior of the embryo (right column Figure 2; Video 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by the imaging data presented in the manuscript and reference to Figure 2 and Video 1C.

claim: The Pt-Ets4 knockdown phenotype is rather similar to that of Pt-dpp.
source: The Pt-Ets4 knockdown phenotype is rather similar to that of Pt-dpp, although cumulus migration/integrity is not affected in Pt-dpp RNAi embryos (Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of the phenotypes and a citation to published work (Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2006).

claim: Cumulus migration/integrity is not affected in Pt-dpp RNAi embryos.
source: The Pt-Ets4 knockdown phenotype is rather similar to that of Pt-dpp, although cumulus migration/integrity is not affected in Pt-dpp RNAi embryos (Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published work (Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2006).

claim: There was no obvious difference in the expression of Pt-dpp in stage 4 control and Pt-Ets4 RNAi embryos.
source: However, there was no obvious difference in the expression of Pt-dpp in stage 4 control and Pt-Ets4 RNAi embryos (Figure 4A and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by the expression data presented in the manuscript and reference to Figure 4A and E.

claim: Pt-dpp appears not to be regulating the expression of Pt-Ets4.
source: Vice versa, Pt-dpp appears not to be regulating the expression of Pt-Ets4 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by the expression data presented in the manuscript and reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Hh signaling seems not to be involved in the regulation of Pt-Ets4 expression.
source: In addition, Hh signaling seems not to be involved in the regulation of Pt-Ets4 expression and Pt-Ets4 appears not to regulate the expression of Pt-ptc within the primary thickening (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by the expression data presented in the manuscript and reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1B and C.

claim: Pt-Ets4 appears not to regulate the expression of Pt-ptc within the primary thickening.
source: In addition, Hh signaling seems not to be involved in the regulation of Pt-Ets4 expression and Pt-Ets4 appears not to regulate the expression of Pt-ptc within the primary thickening (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by the expression data presented in the manuscript and reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1B and C.

claim: Pt-forkhead (Pt-fkh) expression was unaffected in Pt-Ets4 RNAi embryos.
source: We found that Pt-forkhead (Pt-fkh) expression was unaffected (Figure 4B and F)
evidence: The claim is supported by the expression data presented in the manuscript and reference to Figure 4B and F.

claim: The cumulus marker Pt-fascin was slightly down regulated in Pt-Ets4 knockdown embryos.
source: while the cumulus marker Pt-fascin was slightly down regulated, and Pt-hunchback (Pt-hb) was strongly down regulated in Pt-Ets4 knockdown embryos (Figure 4C,D,G and H).
evidence: The claim is supported by the expression data presented in the manuscript and reference to Figure 4C, D, G and H.

claim: Pt-hunchback (Pt-hb) was strongly down regulated in Pt-Ets4 knockdown embryos.
source: while the cumulus marker Pt-fascin was slightly down regulated, and Pt-hunchback (Pt-hb) was strongly down regulated in Pt-Ets4 knockdown embryos (Figure 4C,D,G and H).
evidence: The claim is supported by the expression data presented in the manuscript and reference to Figure 4C, D, G and H.

claim: The EGFP-Pt-Ets4 fusion protein localizes to the nuclei of the injected cells.
source: Our first observation was that the EGFP-Pt-Ets4 fusion protein localizes to the nuclei of the injected cells, suggesting that the nuclear-localization-signal of Pt-Ets4 is functioning normally (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is supported by the imaging data presented in the manuscript and reference to Figure 5A.

claim: The nuclear-localization-signal of Pt-Ets4 is functioning normally.
source: Our first observation was that the EGFP-Pt-Ets4 fusion protein localizes to the nuclei of the injected cells, suggesting that the nuclear-localization-signal of Pt-Ets4 is functioning normally (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that the EGFP-Pt-Ets4 fusion protein localizes to the nuclei.

claim: EGFP-Pt-Ets4 marked cell clones resembled wild-type until stage 4.
source: EGFP-Pt-Ets4 marked cell clones resembled wild-type until stage 4.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental observations presented in the manuscript.

claim: As soon as a dense germ-disc formed, the cell clones expressing EGFP-Pt-Ets4 seemed to move beneath the germ-disc and the EGFP signal became occluded by the opaque cells of the germ-disc.
source: As soon as a dense germ-disc formed, however, the cell clones expressing EGFP-Pt-Ets4 seemed to move beneath the germ-disc and the EGFP signal became occluded by the opaque cells of the germ-disc (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by the imaging data presented in the manuscript and reference to Figure 5B.

claim: Injection of EGFP-NLS constructs alone never resulted in cell clones moving beneath the germ-disc.
source: We have never seen such behavior following injection of EGFP-NLS constructs alone (Figure 5F–F'''), indicating that the change in cell behavior is due to the ectopic expression of Pt-Ets4.
evidence: The claim is supported by the imaging data presented in the manuscript and reference to Figure 5F–F'''.

claim: The change in cell behavior is due to the ectopic expression of Pt-Ets4.
source: We have never seen such behavior following injection of EGFP-NLS constructs alone (Figure 5F–F'''), indicating that the change in cell behavior is due to the ectopic expression of Pt-Ets4.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the comparison of EGFP-Pt-Ets4 and EGFP-NLS injected embryos.

claim: In control embryos (ectopic expression of lynGFP alone), lynGFP strongly marked the cell outlines and cell clones stayed at the surface epithelium of the germ-disc.
source: In control embryos (ectopic expression of lynGFP alone), lynGFP strongly marked the cell outlines and cell clones stayed at the surface epithelium of the germ-disc (Video 2A, Figure 5C–C'').
evidence: The claim is supported by the imaging data presented in the manuscript and reference to Video 2A and Figure 5C–C''.

claim: Cells expressing lynGFP/EGFP-Pt-Ets4 constricted and delaminated shortly after the formation of the germ-disc.
source: Regardless of the position and the shape of the cell clone, cells expressing lynGFP/EGFP-Pt-Ets4 constricted and delaminated shortly after the formation of the germ-disc (Video 2B–D, Figure 5D–D'').
evidence: The claim is supported by the imaging data presented in the manuscript and reference to Video 2B–D and Figure 5D–D''.

claim: The detection of EGFP-Pt-Ets4 cell clones in fixed embryos using an antibody against EGFP confirmed that the labeled cells were below the epithelium of the germ-disc.
source: The detection of EGFP-Pt-Ets4 cell clones in fixed embryos using an antibody against EGFP confirmed that the labeled cells were below the epithelium of the germ-disc (Figure 5E and E').
evidence: The claim is supported by the antibody staining data presented in the manuscript and reference to Figure 5E and E'.

claim: In control embryos (injected with EGFP-NLS alone) the marked cell clones persisted at the surface of the germ-disc.
source: While in the control embryos (injected with EGFP-NLS alone) the marked cell clones persisted at the surface of the germ-disc (Video 3A, Figure 5F and F')
evidence: The claim is supported by the imaging data presented in the manuscript and reference to Video 3A and Figure 5F and F'.

claim: The cell clone expressing both EGFP-NLS and EGFP-Pt-Ets4 delaminated shortly after the formation of the germ-disc.
source: the cell clone expressing both EGFP-NLS and EGFP-Pt-Ets4 delaminated shortly after the formation of the germ-disc (Video 3B, Figure 5G and G').
evidence: The claim is supported by the imaging data presented in the manuscript and reference to Video 3B and Figure 5G and G'.

claim: Germ-disc cells continue to divide and undergo convergent extension during the formation of the germ-band, which causes cell clones to become thin and elongated.
source: As previously shown (Kanayama et al., 2010, Kanayama et al., 2011), germ-disc cells continue to divide and undergo convergent extension during the formation of the germ-band, which causes cell clones to become thin and elongated as seen in our control EGFP-NLS clones (Video 3A, Figure 5F'' and F''').
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published work (Kanayama et al., 2010, Kanayama et al., 2011) and the imaging data presented in the manuscript and reference to Video 3A and Figure 5F'' and F'''.

claim: Cell clones expressing both EGFP-NLS and EGFP-Pt-Ets4 stopped dividing as soon they delaminated.
source: In contrast to this, cell clones expressing both EGFP-NLS and EGFP-Pt-Ets4 stopped dividing as soon they delaminated.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental observations presented in the manuscript.

claim: When the cumulus started to migrate, the delaminated cells of the EGFP-NLS/EGFP-Pt-Ets4 marked cell clone lost contact with each other and spread out underneath the germ-disc/germ-band epithelium.
source: In addition, when the cumulus started to migrate, the delaminated cells of the EGFP-NLS/EGFP-Pt-Ets4 marked cell clone lost contact with each other and spread out underneath the germ-disc/germ-band epithelium (Video 3B, Figure 5G'' and G''').
evidence: The claim is supported by the imaging data presented in the manuscript and reference to Video 3B and Figure 5G'' and G'''.

claim: The observation that delaminated cells of the EGFP-NLS/EGFP-Pt-Ets4 marked cell clone lost contact with each other and spread out was consistent and reproducible in multiple analyzed embryos.
source: This observation was consistent and reproducible in multiple analyzed embryos (Video 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by the imaging data presented in the manuscript and reference to Video 4.

claim: Ets4 expression is sufficient to induce cell delamination and migration in embryos of P. tepidariorum.
source: These results demonstrate that Ets4 expression is sufficient to induce cell delamination and migration in embryos of P. tepidariorum.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Pt-dpp transcripts were not detected in cells ectopically expressing Pt-Ets4.
source: Furthermore, we were not able to detect Pt-dpp transcripts in cells ectopically expressing Pt-Ets4 (Figure 6A and A').
evidence: The claim is supported by the expression data presented in the manuscript and reference to Figure 6A and A'.

claim: Pt-Ets4 is regulating the expression of Pt-hb.
source: In contrast to Pt-dpp, we did find that Pt-Ets4 is regulating the expression of Pt-hb.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Pt-hb expression was nearly absent in Pt-Ets4 RNAi embryos.
source: While Pt-hb expression was nearly absent in Pt-Ets4 RNAi embryos (Figure 4H)
evidence: The claim is supported by the expression data presented in the manuscript and reference to Figure 4H.

claim: Pt-hb transcripts were present in the ectopically Pt-Ets4 positive cell clone.
source: Pt-hb transcripts were present in the ectopically Pt-Ets4 positive cell clone (Figure 6B and B').
evidence: The claim is supported by the expression data presented in the manuscript and reference to Figure 6B and B'.

claim: Pt-twi was detectable within the cell clone that ectopically expressed Pt-Ets4.
source: Indeed, Pt-twi was detectable within the cell clone that ectopically expressed Pt-Ets4 (Figure 6C and C', compare to controls in Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by the expression data presented in the manuscript and reference to Figure 6C and C', and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: In the stage 4 embryos ectopically expressing Pt-Ets4, Pt-twi transcripts were detected within the ectopic Pt-Ets4 expressing cell clone and within the central primary thickening.
source: Interestingly, in the stage 4 embryos ectopically expressing Pt-Ets4, we could not only detect Pt-twi transcripts within the ectopic Pt-Ets4 expressing cell clone, but also within the central primary thickening (Figure 6C').
evidence: The claim is supported by the expression data presented in the manuscript and reference to Figure 6C'.

claim: It was reported that Pt-twi expression is not initiated before the end of stage 5.
source: This comes as a surprise, as it was reported that Pt-twi expression is not initiated before the end of stage 5 (Yamazaki et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published work (Yamazaki et al., 2005).

claim: Pt-twi is expressed in the developing primary thickening of stage 3 and 4 embryos.
source: For this reason, we reanalyzed the full expression series of Pt-twi in wild-type embryos and we were able to confirm that Pt-twi is expressed in the developing primary thickening of stage 3 and 4 embryos (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by the expression data presented in the manuscript and reference to Figure 6—figure supplement 2A–C.

claim: Pt-twi transcripts were no longer detectable in the primary thickening of stage 4 Pt-Ets4 RNAi embryos.
source: Finally, we confirmed the regulation of Pt-twi via Pt-Ets4 by analyzing the expression of Pt-twi in Pt-Ets4 knockdown embryos. Pt-twi transcripts were no longer detectable in the primary thickening of stage 4 Pt-Ets4 RNAi embryos (Figure 6D and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by the expression data presented in the manuscript and reference to Figure 6D and E.

claim: Late segmental mesoderm specification was unaffected in Pt-Ets4 knockdown embryos, as the expression of Pt-twi was unchanged in stage 7 Pt-Ets4 knockdown embryos.
source: However, late segmental mesoderm specification was unaffected, as the expression of Pt-twi was unchanged in stage 7 Pt-Ets4 knockdown embryos (Figure 6—figure supplement 2H–I').
evidence: The claim is supported by the expression data presented in the manuscript and reference to Figure 6—figure supplement 2H–I'.

claim: The formation and migration of the cumulus and later gastrulation events from central and peripheral parts of the germ-disc are two independent processes.
source: This confirms that the formation and migration of the cumulus and later gastrulation events from central and peripheral parts of the germ-disc are two independent processes (Hilbrant et al., 2012; Oda et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript and citations to published work (Hilbrant et al., 2012; Oda et al., 2007).

claim: The activation of Pt-twi and Pt-hb by Pt-Ets4 in cell clones initiated a mesoderm-like cell fate that led to the migratory behavior of the ectopic Pt-Ets4 positive cells.
source: Overall, we suggest that the activation of Pt-twi and Pt-hb by Pt-Ets4 in cell clones initiated a mesoderm-like cell fate that led to the migratory behavior of the ectopic Pt-Ets4 positive cells.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Ets proteins belong to a highly conserved family of transcription factors.
source: Ets proteins belong to a highly conserved family of transcription factors (Laudet et al., 1999)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published work (Laudet et al., 1999).

claim: Ets proteins play roles in a variety of different cellular processes (e.g. growth, migration, differentiation).
source: that play roles in a variety of different cellular processes (e.g. growth, migration, differentiation)
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge.

claim: Ets factors can act as activators or repressors of transcription.
source: and it has been shown that these factors can act as activators or repressors of transcription (Oikawa and Yamada, 2003; Sharrocks et al., 1997; Sharrocks, 2001; Hollenhorst et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published work (Oikawa and Yamada, 2003; Sharrocks et al., 1997; Sharrocks, 2001; Hollenhorst et al., 2011).

claim: In D. melanogaster, Ets4 (also known as Ets98B) is expressed in the oocyte nucleus and the primordial germ cells (PGC).
source: In D. melanogaster, Ets4 (also known as Ets98B) is expressed in the oocyte nucleus and the primordial germ cells (PGC) (Chen et al., 1992; Hsouna et al., 2004)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published work (Chen et al., 1992; Hsouna et al., 2004).

claim: There is evidence that Dm-Ets4 is involved in the migration of the PGCs.
source: and there is evidence that Dm-Ets4 is involved in the migration of the PGCs (Hsouna et al., 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published work (Hsouna et al., 2003).

claim: The mammalian homolog of Ets4, Pdef, is down regulated in invasive and migratory breast tumor cells.
source: Furthermore, the mammalian homolog of Ets4, Pdef, is down regulated in invasive and migratory breast tumor cells (Feldman et al., 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published work (Feldman et al., 2003).

claim: Ets4 regulates migratory cell behavior in different organisms.
source: Together, these reports suggest that Ets4 regulates migratory cell behavior in different organisms.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the cited reports.

claim: In the spider P. tepidariorum, Ets4 is strongly expressed in the migrating cumulus.
source: Here we show that in the spider P. tepidariorum, Ets4 is strongly expressed in the migrating cumulus
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Pt-Ets4 is needed for the integrity of the cumulus, a group of cells, which need to migrate together in order to function normally.
source: and that Pt-Ets4 is needed for the integrity of the cumulus, a group of cells, which need to migrate together in order to function normally.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The ectopic expression of Pt-Ets4 is able to induce cell delamination and cell migration within the ectodermal germ-disc cells.
source: We also show that the ectopic expression of Pt-Ets4 is able to induce cell delamination and cell migration within the ectodermal germ-disc cells (a process that is known as epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition [Thiery et al., 2009; Gilmour et al., 2017]).
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript and citations to published work (Thiery et al., 2009; Gilmour et al., 2017).

claim: Pt-Ets4 likely plays an important role in the migratory behavior of the cumulus.
source: Taken together, these findings suggest that Pt-Ets4 likely plays an important role in the migratory behavior of the cumulus.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: It has been suggested that the cumulus cells of many higher spiders are specified during early embryogenesis and are not secondarily induced after the formation of the germ-disc.
source: It has been suggested that the cumulus cells of many higher spiders are specified during early embryogenesis and are not secondarily induced after the formation of the germ-disc (Edgar et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published work (Edgar et al., 2015).

claim: Pt-Ets4 marks the cells of the developing primary thickening (st. 3 and 4) and of the migrating cumulus.
source: Pt-Ets4 marks the cells of the developing primary thickening (st. 3 and 4) and of the migrating cumulus.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: In P. tepidariorum, cumulus cells are induced before germ-disc formation is complete.
source: Therefore, our results indicate that in P. tepidariorum as well, cumulus cells are induced before germ-disc formation is complete.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Pt-Ets4 cannot be the only factor that is required for the specification of the cells that will develop into the primary thickening (and later into the cumulus).
source: As the primary thickening forms in the absence of Pt-Ets4, Pt-Ets4 cannot be the only factor that is required for the specification of the cells that will develop into the primary thickening (and later into the cumulus).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Pt-Ets4 is sufficient to induce the delamination and migration of ectodermal cells, but it is not sufficient to induce the formation of a fully functional ectopic cumulus.
source: This is supported by our finding that Pt-Ets4 is sufficient to induce the delamination and migration of ectodermal cells, but it is not sufficient to induce the formation of a fully functional ectopic cumulus.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Pt-Ets4 seems not to be involved in the regulation of Pt-dpp itself, as well as several other cumulus marker genes.
source: As shown by our analyses, Pt-Ets4 seems not to be involved in the regulation of Pt-dpp itself, as well as several other cumulus marker genes.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Important factors of the cumulus are missing in the ectopic Pt-Ets4 expression cells.
source: Therefore, important factors of the cumulus are missing in the ectopic Pt-Ets4 expression cells.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The formation of the primary thickening is a process that is buffered via the input of several genes or other unknown mechanisms/factors.
source: Taken together, our findings indicate that the formation of the primary thickening is a process that is buffered via the input of several genes or other unknown mechanisms/factors.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: An intact cumulus is needed to open up the germ-disc and to initiate the formation of a bilaterally symmetric spider embryo.
source: Our results also show that an intact cumulus is needed to open up the germ-disc and to initiate the formation of a bilaterally symmetric spider embryo.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: In the germ-disc of P. tepidariorum embryos, BMP signaling is active from early stage 5.
source: In the germ-disc of P. tepidariorum embryos, BMP signaling is active from early stage 5 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript and reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The germ-disc does not open up before the arrival of the cumulus at the rim of the disc at the end of stage 5 even though the putative receptors are ubiquitously expressed.
source: However, the germ-disc does not open up before the arrival of the cumulus at the rim of the disc at the end of stage 5 even though the putative receptors are ubiquitously expressed.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The establishment of the dorsal field is a precisely timed process.
source: Therefore, the establishment of the dorsal field is a precisely timed process
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: In Pt-Ets4 knockdown embryos the cells of the cumulus may disperse too early, and are no longer able to induce the opening of the germ-disc at the end of stage 5.
source: and it is possible that in Pt-Ets4 knockdown embryos the cells of the cumulus disperse too early, and are no longer able to induce the opening of the germ-disc at the end of stage 5.
evidence: The claim is speculative and based on inference from the experimental data.

claim: The cumulus may signal via cytonemes.
source: An alternative, although not mutually exclusive, explanation involves the fact that the cumulus may signal via cytonemes (Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2003; Hilbrant et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published work (Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2003; Hilbrant et al., 2012).

claim: Cytonemes could be affected in Pt-Ets4 RNAi embryos, as the cumulus cells lose contact with each other.
source: These structures could be affected in Pt-Ets4 RNAi embryos, as the cumulus cells lose contact with each other.
evidence: The claim is speculative and based on inference from the experimental data.

claim: Pt-Ets4 could be involved in regulating the BMP pathway activity at a different level (e.g. protein-protein interactions, protein modifications).
source: Lastly, Pt-Ets4 could be involved in regulating the BMP pathway activity at a different level (e.g. protein-protein interactions, protein modifications)
evidence: The claim is speculative.

claim: The knockdown of Pt-Ets4 could result in a fate change of the cumulus cells before cumulus migration is initiated.
source: or the knockdown of Pt-Ets4 could result in a fate change of the cumulus cells before cumulus migration is initiated.
evidence: The claim is speculative.

claim: Pt-Ets4 is involved in the activation of at least two genes that are expressed within the primary thickening of stage 4 embryos: Pt-hb and Pt-twi.
source: Via both our loss- and gain-of-function experiments, we found that Pt-Ets4 is involved in the activation of at least two genes that are expressed within the primary thickening of stage 4 embryos. These genes are Pt-hb and Pt-twi.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Pt-hb is strongly expressed within the primary thickening of stage 4 embryos.
source: For Pt-hb, it was already shown that this gene is strongly expressed within the primary thickening of stage 4 embryos (Schwager et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published work (Schwager et al., 2009).

claim: The cumulus cells are not endodermal in nature but rather are mesendodermal.
source: This result indicates that the cumulus cells are not endodermal in nature (Oda and Akiyama-Oda, 2008; Hilbrant et al., 2012; Oda et al., 2007) but rather are mesendodermal.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data presented in the manuscript and citations to published work (Oda and Akiyama-Oda, 2008; Hilbrant et al., 2012; Oda et al., 2007).

claim: The cumulus is a fascinating example of a migrating and signaling organizer.
source: The cumulus is a fascinating example of a migrating and signaling organizer.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge in the field.

claim: Cumulus-related dorsoventral patterning defects have been observed in spider embryos that either completely lack BMP signaling or are deficient for cumulus migration.
source: Thus far, cumulus-related dorsoventral patterning defects have been observed in spider embryos that either completely lack BMP signaling or are deficient for cumulus migration (Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2006, Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published work (Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2006, Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2010).

claim: The knockdown of the transcription factor Pt-Ets4 generates a novel dorsoventral phenotype that is dependent on cumulus integrity.
source: Here, we show that the knockdown of the transcription factor Pt-Ets4 generates a novel dorsoventral phenotype that is dependent on cumulus integrity.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Formation of the bilaterally symmetric spider embryo is a precisely timed process that relies on the presence of an intact, migrating and signaling cumulus.
source: Our results show that formation of the bilaterally symmetric spider embryo is a precisely timed process that relies on the presence of an intact, migrating and signaling cumulus.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: BMP signaling is active from early stage 5 onwards.
source: (A–D) The BMP signaling pathway (visualized via pMad antibody staining; false color images) is active from early stage 5 onwards.
evidence: The claim is supported by the antibody staining data presented in the manuscript and reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–D.

claim: The germ-disc does not open up before late stage 5, after the cumulus has reached the rim of the disc.
source: However, the germ-disc does not open up before late stage 5, after the cumulus has reached the rim of the disc.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript.
